# Job Application Pipeline — Design Spec

**Suggested path:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-job-application-pipeline-design.md` in the `ideatub` repo
**Baseline:** Laravel 13, PHP ^8.3, extends the existing `ideatub` app rather than a new repo
**Context:** Built off the usage audit run in Cowork/Cursor (19 Aug 2026), which found job-search work handled ad hoc, CVs regenerated by hand through a bespoke LaTeX pipeline, employer research done inconsistently, and no standing record of application state. IdeaTub already has the working-memory model (`Thought`) and the MCP surface this needs to sit on top of. The save-reliability issue flagged in that audit has been root-caused to the cloud server sleeping, an infra fix, not a blocker for this module (§8).

---

## Executive summary

Add a Job Application module to `ideatub`: a small set of models tracking companies, applications, and interactions, wired into the existing `Thought` system so research and debrief notes stay first-class working-memory entries rather than a separate silo. Exposed over the existing MCP server so the pipeline can be driven from Claude, Cowork, or Cursor without opening the app. Not a new product, an extension of one already running.

Two-stage funnel, deliberately mirroring Scanner's own discover-score-promote shape: a cheap, high-volume **prospects** stage for anything sourced from job boards, LinkedIn, or referrals, and an expensive, low-volume **applications** stage that only a promoted prospect graduates into. This keeps the costly steps, deep research, CV assembly, tracking, debrief, reserved for roles actually worth the effort, the same discipline Scanner already applies to outreach targets rather than treating every lead as a booked meeting.

---

## §1 Problem and goals

The audit identified five gaps: no repeatable research step, CVs rebuilt from scratch per application rather than assembled from fixed source material, no central tracker (state currently lives in scattered markdown files), no debrief/retro step feeding lessons back into future applications, and no MCP-level visibility into pipeline status from chat.

**Goals**

- A lightweight `Prospect` pool for anything sourced but not yet decided on, cheap to populate at volume, no research or document cost until promoted.
- One `Application` record per company/role, carrying stage, dates, salary, and source, created only on promotion from a `Prospect`.
- `Achievement` as a first-class, standalone model, same standing as `Company` or `Thought`, not owned by or scoped to any single `Application`. Managed directly (add, edit, tag, retire) and queried by tag whenever a CV or cover letter needs assembling, whether that's for a specific application or a general CV needed outside the pipeline entirely.
- Research and debrief content stored as `Thought` records (reusing what already exists) and linked bidirectionally to the `Application`, the same pattern already used for linking email research to research threads.
- MCP tools so the pipeline can be queried and updated from any connected AI tool.
- A pipeline board for a fast visual read of where every application stands, built the same way the rest of `ideatub`'s UI is: Blade views off standard controllers, Alpine.js for the inline interactivity, no new frontend framework introduced for this module (§5).
- Document generation owned by `ideatub`, not Cowork's docx skill and not `ai-job-search`'s LaTeX pipeline: CV and cover letter content assembled as markdown from `Achievement` + the research brief, editable in the app before export, exported to PDF through `CvStyle`. `ai-job-search`'s `/apply` becomes a caller against this rather than generating its own documents (§8).
- The whole module ships behind a feature flag (§2c), off by default, so it's not forced into every `ideatub` install and can become a packaged add-on later without restructuring.

## §2 Non-goals

- Not a job-board scraper or auto-apply tool, sourcing stays in `ai-job-search` (§4a).
- No multi-user support in v1, this is a single-user tool for now.

### §2a Format: markdown, not LaTeX

The current CV pipeline, `ideatub`'s bespoke `.tex` sources and custom `tex_to_docx.py` converter, and `ai-job-search`'s own tuned LaTeX templates and reviewer-agent pass, both retired in favour of `ideatub`'s markdown + `CvStyle` pipeline (§8). Reasons: the PDF half was already broken from a missing package in at least one environment, LaTeX source interleaves formatting with content which fights the atomic-bullet model `Achievement` depends on, and a heavily-formatted LaTeX layout is more likely to trip up ATS parsing than a plain single-column export. The existing `.tex` files aren't parsed or imported (§8), they're just reference material while `Achievement` is entered manually.

### §2b Visual consistency: styling lives in one place

Content (`Achievement` bullets, research/debrief `Thought`s) stays plain markdown throughout the pipeline. Styling is applied exactly once, at document assembly, never per-document. This is the direct fix for font/size drift: the previous approach hand-touched 52 regenerated files in one session, so drift was structural, not accidental.

A single style definition, `App\Services\Documents\CvStyle` (a constants class, not a database row, there is one style, not several to pick between):

- **One font family** across the whole document, no mixed serif/sans: **Helvetica**. ATS-safe, unremarkable in the right way. Exporting straight to PDF (§8) rather than through Word sidesteps the old Windows/Arial-substitution risk entirely, PDFs embed the font directly, so what's previewed in `ideatub` is exactly what ships, no viewer-side substitution to double-check.
- **Three sizes maximum**: name/header, section headings, body text. Job titles, dates, and bullet text all sit at body size, distinction comes from bold or layout, not a fourth size.
- **Line height and heading spacing fixed once**, the other common source of inconsistency even when font and size are already controlled.

Every CV and cover letter generated by the pipeline references this one definition, applied as CSS against a markdown-derived HTML template. Changing the look means changing `CvStyle`, not touching any generated document. Recommend `spatie/browsershot` (headless Chrome) for the markdown/HTML → PDF step over `dompdf`/`mpdf`, better CSS fidelity for controlling exact type and spacing, which is the whole point of `CvStyle` existing.

### §2c Optional module, feature-gated

Ships behind `config/features.php`, the same convention every existing optional feature in `ideatub` already uses (`file_upload`, `working_memory_ui`, `attention_pulse`, the `memory_graph_*` set), not a new mechanism invented for this module:

- Add `'job_search' => env('FEATURE_JOB_SEARCH', false),` to `config/features.php`. Off by default, matching every other flag in that file.
- New `App\Http\Middleware\EnsureJobSearchEnabled`, mirroring the existing `Ensure*Enabled` middlewares (`EnsureWorkingMemoryUiEnabled`, `EnsureAttentionPulseEnabled`), applied to the job-pipeline route group.
- Controllers and the new MCP tool handlers (§6, inside `McpController`) also check `config('features.job_search')` directly at the point of use, the same belt-and-braces pattern `ImportController` uses for `file_upload`, so a direct route hit or an MCP call while the flag's off fails the same way the UI does.
- Nav link to the job pipeline only renders when the flag is on, same conditional pattern the layout already uses elsewhere for `working_memory_ui`.

This is an env-level toggle, not a per-user database setting or a Filament-style admin switch, `ideatub` doesn't have either of those today and this module doesn't need to be the first thing that introduces them. Turning it off doesn't touch data, prospects, applications, achievements, and their linked `Thought`s all stay intact, it just stops the routes, nav, and MCP tools from responding.

**Future packaging.** `ideatub` already has Cashier wired up with Pro and Lifetime checkout (`PricingController`, `routes/web.php`), so when this becomes a paid add-on rather than a flag anyone can flip in their own `.env`, the natural upgrade is swapping what `EnsureJobSearchEnabled` checks, from the static config value to the user's subscription state, e.g. `$request->user()->subscribed('pro')` or a dedicated entitlement check. One middleware, one condition to change, not a rearchitecture.

## §3 Data model

```
job_prospects
  id, company, role_title, source (linkedin, job_board, referral, direct),
  url, salary_signal (nullable), fit_score (nullable int, 0-100),
  status (enum: new, scored, shortlisted, dismissed, promoted),
  discovered_at, scored_at, notes, promoted_application_id (nullable FK -> applications.id)

companies
  id, name, website, notes, research_thought_id (nullable FK -> thoughts.id)

applications
  id, company_id (FK), job_prospect_id (nullable FK -> job_prospects.id), role_title,
  stage (enum), source, salary_min, salary_max,
  applied_at, last_activity_at, research_thought_id (FK -> thoughts.id, nullable),
  cv_markdown (nullable, editable draft), cover_letter_markdown (nullable, editable draft),
  cv_pdf_path (nullable), cover_letter_pdf_path (nullable),
  cv_exported_at (nullable), cover_letter_exported_at (nullable),
  created_at, updated_at

application_stage enum:
  researching, applied, screening, interviewing, offer, rejected, withdrawn

interactions
  id, application_id (FK), type (enum: interview, follow_up, rejection, offer, note),
  occurred_at, summary, debrief_thought_id (nullable FK -> thoughts.id)

achievements  (model: Achievement — standalone, not scoped to any application, see §1)
  id, tag (string, e.g. "laravel", "leadership", "mcp"), bullet_text (markdown/plain text),
  times_used (int), last_used_at, retired_at (nullable, soft-retire rather than delete)
```

`bullet_text` is markdown, not LaTeX. LaTeX is the source of the current CV but not the target format for anything new, see §2a.

Reuses the existing `Thought` model for anything narrative (research briefs, debrief notes) rather than duplicating a notes system. `research_thought_id` and `debrief_thought_id` are the same bidirectional-linking pattern already built for email-research linking, applied here instead of reinvented. `job_prospects` deliberately does not get a `Thought` link, it's meant to stay cheap and disposable; a research `Thought` only gets created once a prospect is promoted.

`job_prospects.notes` is a plain free-text field, deliberately not a `Thought`, for jotting things down while a prospect is still cheap (why it caught your eye, a recruiter's throwaway comment, a salary hint from a LinkedIn post) before it's worth the weight of a full research entry. On promotion this is not dropped: if `notes` is non-empty, it seeds the initial content of the `Application`'s `research_thought_id` (a `Thought` is created at promotion time rather than left until the Research stage, pre-filled with the prospect's notes so nothing typed early is lost).

`cv_markdown` / `cover_letter_markdown` are the editable drafts, assembled from `Achievement` + the research brief at the Build stage, then hand-edited in `ideatub` before export. `cv_pdf_path` / `cover_letter_pdf_path` and the matching `*_exported_at` timestamps only get set by the explicit export action (§5, §6), never automatically on save, so a markdown edit after export leaves a stale PDF on disk rather than silently regenerating one mid-edit. Whether to surface that staleness in the UI (a "markdown changed since export" flag) is a nice-to-have, not required for v1.

## §4 Pipeline stages

Two funnels. Sourcing is cheap and high-volume; the application pipeline is expensive and only runs for what's been promoted.

| Stage | Coding equivalent | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Source | — | A `Prospect` is created (manually, or by an automated scan, see §4a) for anything worth tracking, no research yet |
| Score | — | A lightweight fit pass, salary signal, role-match heuristics, maybe a quick job-research pass in a cheaper mode, sets `fit_score` and moves status to `scored` |
| Shortlist / dismiss | — | Manual call (or an AI recommendation above a threshold that gets confirmed): `shortlisted` prospects are worth pursuing, `dismissed` ones are archived without further cost |
| **Promote** | — | A shortlisted `Prospect` becomes an `Application`, `promoted_application_id` set on the prospect, `job_prospect_id` set on the application, `notes` carried over into a seeded research `Thought` (§3). Normally starts at `researching`; the fast-path "Mark Applied" action (§5) promotes straight to `applied` with `applied_at` set, for anything applied to outside the tool that just needs logging |
| Research | Spec | Run job-research against the company/role, save the brief as a `Thought`, link it to the `Application` |
| Fit check | Plan | Match the brief against the CV and `Achievement`, tag which bullets apply |
| Build | Implement | Assemble tailored CV/cover letter markdown from `Achievement` + the research brief, edit in `ideatub`, export to PDF via `CvStyle`, record markdown and PDF paths on the `Application` |
| Log | Commit | `Application` moves to `applied`, `applied_at` set |
| Track | — | Stage updates as responses come in (`screening`, `interviewing`, `offer`, `rejected`) |
| Debrief | Review | On `rejected` or after an interview, prompt for a short retro, saved as a `Thought`, linked via `debrief_thought_id`, and any reusable insight fed back into `Achievement` |

### §4a Sourcing, the Scanner parallel

Scanner already solves this exact shape for outreach: discover candidates, score them, only invest in the ones that clear a bar (`DispatchMarketScanRefresh` periodically rescans and rescores rather than someone manually vetting every lead). The prospects stage here is the same pattern applied to job hunting, deliberately, rather than reinvented. Two ways to populate it:

- Manual: add a listing seen on a job board or LinkedIn as a `Prospect` directly, via the `add_prospect` MCP tool (§6) from chat, for anything spotted outside the pipeline.
- **Primary path: reuse `ai-job-search`, don't rebuild it.** `~/Sites/ai-job-search` (MadsLorentzen's open-source Claude Code job-search framework, forked with five UK portals added: Reed, TotalJobs, WeWorkRemotely, CWJobs, LaraJobs, on top of the original LinkedIn/Danish set) already does this stage: ten tuned portal scrapers, dedup, and a fit-scoring pass, run through `/scrape` and `/rank`. Not theoretical, it has real outcomes behind it (`job_search_tracker.csv`, `documents/applications/`). Reimplementing that as Laravel scrapers would mean rebuilding and then maintaining ten portal integrations that already exist, are upstream-maintained (`tools/check_upstream_updates.py`), and are already tuned against real applied/interviewed/rejected results, not worth duplicating for its own sake.

  Instead: register `ideatub`'s MCP server in `ai-job-search`'s `.claude/settings.json`, then extend the `job-scraper` skill (`/scrape`) and `/rank` to call `add_prospect` / `score_prospect` against `ideatub` as part of their existing write-state step, in place of (or alongside, during a transition) writing to `job_scraper/seen_jobs.json`. Dedup stays local to `ai-job-search`, cheap and URL-keyed either way, but the resulting `Prospect` record lands in `ideatub`.

Deliberately not sharing tables with Scanner itself, see §8, even though the pattern is identical, Scanner is a live client-facing product and personal job data shouldn't live in its schema. `ai-job-search` is a different case, personal-scale by design, so feeding it into `ideatub` directly is fine.

## §5 UI

No Filament, no Livewire, `ideatub` doesn't run either. Standard controller-plus-Blade, the same pattern `ProjectController`/`projects.*` already use (route-model binding, `$this->authorize`, `view('job_pipeline.*', [...])`), with Alpine.js for the bits that need interactivity without a full page reload, matching how the rest of the app already handles that (`resources/js/app.js`). New policies (`ApplicationPolicy`, `ProspectPolicy`, `AchievementPolicy`) follow the existing `app/Policies` convention. Entire section sits behind the `EnsureJobSearchEnabled` middleware (§2c).

**`JobApplicationController`** (or similarly named, final name a Task 5 detail): `index` returns `job_pipeline.applications.board`, a Kanban-style board grouped by `stage`, plus a list view sortable by `last_activity_at`. `show` returns `job_pipeline.applications.show`, the `Application` detail page, with `Company` and `Interaction` shown as related records loaded off the model, not separate resources, just eager-loaded relations rendered inline, the same way `ProjectController::show` already loads `thoughts`/`contextThought` onto one page.

The `Application` detail page also carries the document editor: two markdown `<textarea>` fields (`cv_markdown`, `cover_letter_markdown`) with an Alpine-driven live preview panel rendered through `CvStyle`'s CSS, and an **Export PDF** button per document, a POST route that renders the current markdown to `cv_pdf_path` / `cover_letter_pdf_path` and stamps `*_exported_at`. Editing never auto-exports, exporting is a separate explicit request so a mid-edit draft is never accidentally shipped.

**`JobProspectController`**: `index` returns `job_pipeline.prospects.index`, a plain list (no board, volume's too high and low-effort for a Kanban to earn its keep here), with a `notes` `<textarea>` per row that autosaves on blur via a small Alpine/fetch call to a `PATCH` endpoint, and three one-click row actions, each a small POST form (or Alpine `fetch`, no full reload) hitting a dedicated controller action:

- **Shortlist** — sets `status` to `shortlisted`. Marks it worth pursuing without committing to the full pipeline yet.
- **Mark Applied** — the fast path for anything already applied to outside the tool (a quick LinkedIn Easy Apply, a referral submitted on the spot) that just needs logging rather than the full research → build → log sequence. Calls `promote_prospect` with the stage override (§4, §6): creates the `Application` directly at `applied`, `applied_at` set to now, `notes` still carried into the seeded research `Thought` so context isn't lost just because the pipeline was skipped.
- **Dismiss** — sets `status` to `dismissed`, since a prospect list without a way to archive dead leads just accumulates noise.

**`AchievementController`**: `index` returns `job_pipeline.achievements.index`, independent of `Application`, filterable by `tag` via a query-string filter, `times_used`/`last_used_at` shown so it's obvious which bullets are overused or stale. Standard add/edit/retire forms, no application needs to be open to manage the bank.

## §6 MCP surface

New tools alongside the existing `capture_thought` / `get_working_memory` set:

- `add_prospect(company, role_title, source, url?)` — cheap, fire-and-forget from chat
- `score_prospect(prospect_id, fit_score, notes?)`
- `promote_prospect(prospect_id, stage?)` — creates the `Application`, carries `notes` into a seeded research `Thought`, returns its id. Defaults to `researching`; pass `applied` for the fast-path "already applied elsewhere" case (mirrors the Mark Applied button, §5)
- `create_application(company, role_title, source)` — direct entry, bypassing prospects, for roles that don't need a sourcing step (e.g. a direct approach or referral straight into a live conversation)
- `update_application_stage(application_id, stage, note?)`
- `log_interaction(application_id, type, summary)`
- `get_pipeline_status()` — returns all open prospects and applications grouped by stage
- `search_applications(query)`
- `add_achievement(tag, bullet_text)` — grows the bank directly from a conversation, independent of any application
- `retire_achievement(achievement_id)`
- `get_achievements(tags?)` — queries `Achievement` for CV assembly from chat, works standalone or as part of the Build stage
- `generate_application_documents(application_id)` — assembles `cv_markdown` / `cover_letter_markdown` from `Achievement` + the research brief, saves as the draft, returns the markdown for review before export. This is the tool `ai-job-search`'s `/apply` calls instead of generating its own LaTeX (§8): it requests tailored content per application from `ideatub` rather than owning generation itself
- `export_application_pdf(application_id, document)` — renders the current (possibly hand-edited) markdown to PDF via `CvStyle`, `document` is `cv` or `cover_letter`, mirrors the Export PDF button (§5)

Every tool above checks `config('features.job_search')` first (§2c) and returns a clear "feature disabled" error rather than executing when it's off. This is what closes the loop identified in the tool-fit ranking: pipeline status and updates become reachable from Claude, Cowork, or Cursor without opening the app, the same way Scanner's prospect data already is.

## §7 Build plan

Task-by-task, each as its own worktree per the existing convention.

- [ ] **Task 1** — migrations: `job_prospects`, `companies`, `applications`, `interactions`, `achievements`
- [ ] **Task 2** — `job_search` feature flag: `config/features.php` entry, `EnsureJobSearchEnabled` middleware, matching the existing `Ensure*Enabled` pattern (§2c). Built early so every task after this gates behind it from the start rather than retrofitting
- [ ] **Task 3** — models + relationships, `Achievement` as a standalone model (§1), `application_stage` and `prospect_status` enums, factory/seeders for local testing
- [ ] **Task 4** — bidirectional linking to `Thought` (reuse existing linking service rather than duplicating it)
- [ ] **Task 5** — MCP tools (§6), each checking `config('features.job_search')` first, tested against a local MCP client before wiring into Claude
- [ ] **Task 6** — controllers, Blade views, and policies: pipeline board, prospects list (inline `notes`, Shortlist/Mark Applied/Dismiss row actions, §5), `Achievement`'s own index, and the `Application` document editor (markdown fields + Export PDF action, §5), all behind the Task 2 middleware
- [ ] **Task 7** — seed `Achievement` manually via its index view and `add_achievement`, using the old CV `.tex` files as reference only, no import parser (§8)
- [ ] **Task 8** — promotion logic: `promote_prospect` creates the `Application`, copies over company/role/source, sets `job_prospect_id`, seeds `research_thought_id` from `notes` when present, honours the optional stage override for the fast-applied path
- [ ] **Task 9** — document generation service: markdown assembly from `Achievement` + research brief (`generate_application_documents`), `CvStyle` as CSS, `spatie/browsershot` for the HTML → PDF export (`export_application_pdf`)
- [ ] **Task 10** — `ai-job-search` integration: register `ideatub`'s MCP server in its `.claude/settings.json`, wire `/scrape` and `/rank` to `add_prospect`/`score_prospect` (§4a), wire `/apply` to `generate_application_documents` in place of its own LaTeX generation (§8)
- [ ] **Task 11** — dry run: one real prospect end to end, sourced via `ai-job-search` → score → shortlist → promote → research → fit check → build (markdown, edit, export) → log → debrief, plus a check that flipping `FEATURE_JOB_SEARCH` off cleanly hides everything without touching data

Review gate after each task per the usual pattern: code-quality review, spec-compliance review against this doc, final review before merge.

## §8 Decisions

All five open questions from the prior draft are resolved:

- **Save reliability.** Root cause identified: the cloud server sleeping (idle/scale-to-zero on the hosting side), not an application-level flakiness bug. Fix is infra-side, an always-on tier or a scheduled keep-alive ping, not a data-model or sequencing concern. Doesn't block this module's build order, no longer a gate.
- **`Achievement` seeding.** Manual, not an import parser. Entered through the `add_achievement` MCP tool and its own index view (§5, §6), both already in scope. The old CV `.tex` files stay useful as reference while entering, no parser gets built against them (§2a, §7 Task 7).
- **Document generation.** Owned entirely by `ideatub`, not Cowork's docx skill, not `ai-job-search`'s LaTeX pipeline. Content is markdown (`cv_markdown` / `cover_letter_markdown`, §3), editable in the app, exported to PDF on an explicit action via `CvStyle` (§2b, §5, §7 Task 9).
- **Module boundary.** Reconfirmed: this entire module, prospects included, lives in `ideatub`. Scanner is referenced only as a pattern to mirror (discover-score-promote), never as a place to store data, and `ai-job-search` is an integration point, not a home for any of this data (§4a). No tables, migrations, or MCP tools in this spec touch the `nthdesigns-scanner` repo.
- **`ai-job-search` overlap.** Resolved in `ideatub`'s favour: `ai-job-search`'s `/apply` stops generating its own LaTeX and becomes a caller, it requests tailored content per application via `generate_application_documents` (§6), `ideatub` customises the CV and cover letter from `Achievement` and the job brief and hands back the markdown/PDF. `ai-job-search` keeps sourcing (§4a), submission, and outcome tracking on its own side; `ideatub` owns fit-check, research linkage, and document content (§7 Task 10).
- **Optional module.** The whole thing ships behind the `job_search` feature flag (§2c), off by default, matching how every other optional `ideatub` feature already works, and with a clear upgrade path to a paid add-on later via the Cashier subscription check already noted in §2c.

## §9 Success criteria

- A real application goes through research → build → log → debrief without touching a markdown file or the LaTeX pipeline.
- Pipeline status is answerable from a single MCP query rather than checking scattered files.
- At least one debrief insight demonstrably changes a later CV or cover letter, proving the feedback loop actually closes.
